A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDD framework and retain the original synthetic translation task. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. V1 has no appendix; v2 includes complete supplementary Appendices A–B.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic translation experiments, including supervision-dependent MAE results in Table II, bridge translation examples and condition-noise sensitivity results.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic, face-translation and medical-imaging experiments, with additional ablations, sampling analyses, diversity measurements and computational results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The central independent per-domain noise formulation and conditional inference procedure remain. V2 Algorithm 1 adds a random conditional mask that keeps selected domains clean during training; removing this step defines MDD[RAND]. This is a bounded training refinement, distinct from the expanded implementation description.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only the synthetic cube/pyramid/icosphere dataset. V2 retains it under the name BL3NDT and adds CelebAMask-HQ face, sketch and segmentation tasks and BraTS 2020 MRI modality completion and tumor segmentation. The supplement also evaluates unconditional joint face/sketch/mask generation.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated ControlNet[N] comparisons on all three datasets (Appendix B.6), substantially broadening the comparison methods. V1's NoisyCond-O and UMM-CSGM-O variants using −1 for missing views disappear. NoisyCond becomes MSDM†, while the noise-filled adaptations remain under revised names; these renamings are not new baselines.

E3.justification: For the retained synthetic experiments, the reported batch size changes from 32 to 128 and plateau-based learning-rate reduction by 0.5 becomes decay by 0.75 every ten epochs. V2 adds 0% fully supervised training examples, dataset-specific sampling protocols, LPIPS/SSIM/PSNR/Jaccard evaluations, and sampler/step-count comparisons. These extend and revise the evaluation design.

E4.justification: V1's condition-noise sweep is retained in Appendix B.1. V2 adds MDD[NOISY] and MDD[RAND] component ablations, diversity–fidelity analysis, scheduler sensitivity, generation-trajectory comparisons, and tests reducing available MRI inputs from four to one (Section 4.5.2 and Appendices B.2–B.4). These investigate mechanisms and robustness beyond the original analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix B.5 newly specifies that generation times are averaged over 100 runs. This adds repeated-measurement reporting for computational results, not evidence of increased training repetitions. Accuracy results in both versions lack reported seed variation, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Synthetic results are replaced: MDD's fully supervised MAE changes from 0.06096 in v1 Table II to 0.0316 in v2 Table 2 after accounting for its scale, under revised training settings. Extensive real-data and diagnostic results are added. The new BraTS T1 P50% comparison is mixed: ControlNet[N] has higher PSNR than MDD (23.968 versus 22.928), but lower SSIM (0.832 versus 0.892; Table 11).

T1.justification: The Introduction corrects P(D) from 'partitions' to the power set and explicitly identifies 2^L source/complement configurations. This is a limited formal correction. The basic diffusion mathematics remains, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs; v2's additional displayed equations largely unpack existing algorithmic operations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains flexible, semi-supervised multi-domain diffusion. V2's abstract narrows the novelty positioning: arbitrary-domain translation is acknowledged as shared with prior approaches, while inherent semi-supervised handling is emphasized. Its conclusion also adds an explicit claim of superior information fusion across modalities.

C2.justification: V2 expands explanations of noisy-conditioning failures, segmentation behavior and diversity–fidelity tradeoffs. Its new limitations section discusses the shared fusion bottleneck, parameter scaling, difficulties with heterogeneous modalities and absent human evaluation. These substantially extend v1's bridge-error discussion and brief future-work remarks.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands reproducibility information, documenting optimizer parameters, EMA, training budgets, early stopping, preprocessing, ControlNet training and architecture/time-embedding details. Appendix B.5 identifies timing hardware and measurement procedures. V2 also replaces v1's 'code will be made available' footnote with a concrete repository address.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning beyond the original clean/noisy diffusion comparison, adding discussions of StarGAN, fixed-direction ControlNet, diffusion-inpainting mechanisms and mixture-of-experts fusion for scalability. It also refines the novelty attribution toward inherent semi-supervision. Publication-year and venue updates for retained references do not constitute these changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Existing implementation material moves into Appendix A, the original noise-strategy study moves into Appendix B.1, and the experimental narrative is reorganized by dataset. Dedicated limitations and broader-impact sections further change the document structure.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column presentation with a single-column layout, restructures comparison tables and adds architecture, generation-trajectory, diversity and medical-result displays. Existing figures are also revised or relocated: v1's noise-strategy Figures 6–7 become v2 Figures 12–13, rather than new analyses.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's principal evidential weakness—validation confined to synthetic data—through face translation and medical modality-completion experiments. Component ablations, robustness analyses and fuller implementation details substantially strengthen support and reproducibility. Reporting problems remain, notably the apparent interchange of T1 baseline rows between Tables 4 and 13 and absent accuracy uncertainty estimates, but they do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and explanatory depth.
